articles.title: Shaheen Afridi surpasses Waqar Younis and Shoaib Akhtar, becomes fastest Pakistan pacer to reach ODI wickets milestone
articles.summary: Pakistan left-arm pacer Shaheen Shah Afridi reached a major milestone in ODI cricket on Sunday during the fourth match of the tri-series against England
articles.body: Pakistan left-arm pacer Shaheen Shah Afridi reached a major milestone in ODI cricket on Sunday during the fourth match of the tri-series against England at Gaddafi Stadium.Bowling first, Shaheen dismissed England opener Tom Banton in the first over to claim his 150th wicket in the 50-over format. The 26-year-old became the second-fastest Pakistani bowler overall and the fastest Pakistani fast bowler to reach the landmark.Shaheen achieved the feat in his 80th ODI, two matches more than former Pakistan spinner Saqlain Mushtaq, who holds the record for the fastest Pakistani bowler to take 150 wickets, having reached the milestone in 78 matches.However, Shaheen went past Pakistan pace greats Waqar Younis and Shoaib Akhtar, who both took 91 matches to claim 150 ODI wickets, to become the country's fastest fast bowler to reach the mark.Fastest Pakistani bowlers to 150 ODI wicketsSaqlain Mushtaq — 78 matchesShaheen Shah Afridi — 80 matches*Waqar Younis — 91 matchesShoaib Akhtar — 91 matchesSaeed Ajmal — 93 matchesUmar Gul — 104 matchesGlobally, Shaheen is the joint-fourth fastest bowler to take 150 ODI wickets. Nepal's Sandeep Lamichhane holds the record, having reached the milestone in 73 matches, followed by Mitchell Starc (77) and Mushtaq (78).Shaheen shares the fourth spot with Afghanistan's Rashid Khan and India's Mohammed Shami, who also took 80 ODIs to complete 150 wickets.The Pakistan captain added another wicket to his tally soon after, dismissing England batter Joe Root, who was caught at backward point.Shaheen won the toss and elected to field against England in the ODI tri-series match.England are looking for their first win of the tournament after losing to Pakistan by 87 runs in their opening match. They then saw Sri Lanka chase down 430 at Rawalpindi, the second-highest total successfully chased in ODI cricket, despite Harry Brook scoring the fastest double century in the format off 114 balls.Pakistan, meanwhile, began the tri-series with a 37-run win over Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi and also defended their total against the same opponents. They made two changes to their playing XI for Sunday's match, the first of the tournament's Lahore leg.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson set for scans after injury concerns hit New Zealand ahead of 3rd T20I
articles.summary: New Zealand's preparations for the remainder of the T20I series against India have suffered a setback, with fast bowlers Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson
articles.body: New Zealand's preparations for the remainder of the T20I series against India have suffered a setback, with fast bowlers Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson set to undergo scans to determine the extent of their injuries. While Henry has been ruled out of the remaining matches, Ferguson will miss the third T20I in Wellington, leaving the visitors to reassess their pace-bowling options as they navigate a demanding white-ball schedule.Head coach Rob Walter confirmed that the duo would undergo scans on Tuesday, with the team hoping for positive news ahead of the subsequent ODI and Test assignments.Henry picked up the injury during Saturday's match, bowling just two overs before leaving the field with a tight calf, as described by captain Mitchell Santner. The pacer will remain in Christchurch before joining New Zealand's ODI squad in Auckland on November 2, two days before the first ODI.Ferguson, meanwhile, was withdrawn from the field as a precautionary measure. He will sit out the third T20I but is expected to return for the final two matches of the series in Auckland and Hamilton."Those two are being assessed. They'll go for some scans on Tuesday after the public holiday. We'll have some more information as to where things stand. Obviously, like always, we're just hoping for the best. That'll allow for the quickest turnaround," Walter said in a video shared by New Zealand Cricket (NZC) on Sunday.Walter also explained that New Zealand had planned to rotate their fast bowlers throughout the series to manage workloads and ensure they were prepared for the upcoming five-match ODI series and two-Test assignment.As part of that strategy, Adam Milne missed the previous match, while Kyle Jamieson is set to feature in the third T20I before remaining in Wellington to represent Canterbury in a Ford Trophy match against Basin Reserve opposition at the Basin Reserve. Blair Tickner will join the squad for the final three T20Is, while Josh Clarkson is expected to come in for the last two matches. Matt Fisher will also join the team as cover for the Wellington T20I.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Big shake-up in Bangladesh cricket: BCB removes Mohammad Ashraful as batting coach days before Test series
articles.summary: The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has removed Mohammad Ashraful as the men's team's batting coach, with High Performance coach Mohammad Salahuddin set to
articles.body: The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has removed Mohammad Ashraful as the men's team's batting coach, with High Performance coach Mohammad Salahuddin set to take over on an interim basis.Ashraful was appointed to the role in November 2025. In a media release, the BCB said he would be moved to another position within the board, while Salahuddin would remain in charge of the batting unit until a permanent replacement is appointed. The board did not provide details about Ashraful's new role.Salahuddin had previously served as Bangladesh's assistant coach and was in charge of the batting unit before Ashraful replaced him.Ashraful was part of one of the most memorable moments in Bangladesh cricket history. At just 20, he scored a century to help Bangladesh pull off a stunning upset against Australia in 2005.He went on to play 177 ODIs, scoring 3,468 runs, the fifth-highest tally for Bangladesh. He also featured in 61 Tests, becoming the youngest player to score a Test century, and played 23 T20Is. Ashraful remained active in domestic cricket as recently as two years ago.However, his playing career also had its share of setbacks. In 2013, he was handed a lengthy ban from all BCB-related cricket activities for his involvement in match-fixing in the Bangladesh Premier League. He returned to the fold three years later and eventually moved into coaching.Ashraful's contract as batting coach was subsequently extended until February next year.Bangladesh's next assignment is a two-Test series against the West Indies, starting on October 28 in Mirpur. The team recently lost to Afghanistan in the final of the UAE ODI tri-series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Mumbai's bid to extend their winning run in the Ranji Trophy will have to continue without the services of experienced all-rounder Shardul Thakur, who
articles.body: Mumbai's bid to extend their winning run in the Ranji Trophy will have to continue without the services of experienced all-rounder Shardul Thakur, who remains short of full fitness following a finger injury. Mumbai have made a dominant start to their campaign, but will be without one of their key players when they take on Haryana in an Elite Group D clash at the BKC Complex from Monday.Thakur has been sidelined since sustaining the injury during a training session ahead of the season's opening round. Although the 34-year-old has resumed training with the Mumbai squad, he has yet to regain full match fitness. He was initially expected to miss at least the first two rounds, with the team hopeful of having him available for the Haryana fixture.Mumbai decide against rushing Thakur's returnMumbai have decided against rushing Thakur back into action and are set to field the same squad that secured a comprehensive victory over Himachal Pradesh in Bilaspur in their previous outing, according to cricinfo.Thakur last featured in the Duleep Trophy quarter-final for West Zone against North Zone in late August. He bowled 14 overs, picked up one wicket and scored 10 runs in his only innings as West Zone suffered a 54-run defeat.While continuing his recovery and working towards a return to competitive cricket, Thakur is also set to take up commentary duties for some of India's ongoing T20 Internationals against New Zealand.Mumbai ride on dominant start to Ranji campaignMumbai have made an impressive start to their Ranji Trophy campaign, registering consecutive innings victories to collect 14 points and move to the top of Elite Group D.They began with an innings-and-155-run win over Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium before defeating Himachal Pradesh by an innings and 97 runs in Bilaspur. Mumbai will look to maintain that momentum as they prepare for a tougher challenge against another in-form side.Haryana clash set to test group leadersMumbai will also be without vice-captain Ayush Mhatre, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while opener Yashasvi Jaiswal is in New Zealand ahead of the upcoming Test series after featuring in the India A series. articles.title: Australia get Cameron Green boost ahead of series-deciding Test against South Africa, set to return as specialist batter
articles.summary: Australia have received a timely boost ahead of the series-deciding third Test against South Africa, with all-rounder Cameron Green declaring himself fit
articles.body: Australia have received a timely boost ahead of the series-deciding third Test against South Africa, with all-rounder Cameron Green declaring himself fit for the Cape Town encounter. However, the 27-year-old is expected to return as a specialist batter, having yet to receive clearance to bowl following an abdominal muscle injury.Green's availability comes at a crucial juncture for Australia, who suffered a heavy defeat in the second Test to allow South Africa to level the three-match series at 1-1. With the series on the line, the visitors will hope his return strengthens a batting order that struggled in Gqeberha.Green prefers No. 4 or 5, but remains flexibleGreen has identified No. 4 or No. 5 as his preferred batting positions, although he remains willing to adapt to the team's requirements."I think I'm well suited at four and five," Green said, while adding that he was happy to move up and down the order depending on what Australia needed.The all-rounder has batted at several positions during his international career, from No. 3 to No. 8. His experience in the middle order could prove valuable as Australia look to improve their batting performance in the series decider.However, Australia's team combination remains a key consideration. Matt Renshaw impressed in the opening Test while filling in for Green, scoring 190 and 82, strengthening his claims for a place in the side. Green's return could therefore prompt a reshuffle as the selectors weigh their options.Green recovers quicker than expected from injuryGreen sustained an abdominal muscle tear during Australia's ODI series against South Africa on September 30. The injury ruled him out of the first two Tests, but his recovery has progressed faster than he initially anticipated."I'm all good to go. Pretty surprised with how quickly it's actually healed, or how functional I feel only a few weeks after," Green said.Despite his improved fitness, Green has not yet been cleared to bowl. Australia are therefore likely to use him primarily for his batting contribution rather than as a full all-round option.Australia and South Africa level at 1-1Australia won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs to take the early advantage in the series. Matt Renshaw starred with scores of 190 and 82, while Josh Hazlewood claimed six wickets for 49 runs in South Africa's second innings.South Africa responded emphatically in the second Test at Gqeberha, winning by an innings and 31 runs to level the series. The hosts posted 425/9 declared in their first innings, led by captain Temba Bavuma's 179 and a century from Tristan Stubbs.Australia were dismissed for 99 in their first innings before Travis Head's 121 helped them reach 295 in the second, but it was not enough to prevent defeat.The third and final Test begins on October 27 at Newlands in Cape Town, with both teams chasing a series victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
